image_description: A wooden staircase interior featuring a prominent bannister system. The handrail is dark polished wood with a curved newel post at the landing. The balusters are slender, vertical wooden spindles painted white or light cream, contrasting with the dark handrail and yellow-painted wall/stringer. The stairs themselves have wooden treads. A small mirror hangs on the wall in the background.

artifact_observations.location: Base of the central newel post/balusters near the floor
artifact_observations.reasoning: The connection point where the vertical spindles meet the stair tread/stringer is slightly indistinct. There is a minor 'melting' or blurring effect where the white paint of the balusters meets the yellow wall/wood, lacking sharp geometric definition typical of real carpentry.
The oval mirror on the back wall has a slightly irregular shape, and the door frame behind it seems to warp subtly, suggesting minor geometric inconsistency in the background elements.
The yellow wall has a very smooth, airbrushed texture that lacks the subtle imperfections of plaster or paint, appearing slightly synthetic.
